Use FastAPI's **lifespan events** to run code once at startup. You can define logic (code) that should be executed before the application **starts up**. This means that this code will be executed **once**, **before** the application **starts receiving requests**.[1] The docs describe your exact case: loading the model can **take quite some time**, because it has to read a lot of **data from disk**. So you don't want to do it for every request.[1]

**Why not load it at module level?** That would also mean that it would **load the model** even if you are just running a simple automated test, then that test would be **slow** because it would have to wait for the model to load before being able to run an independent part of the code.[1]

**Cleanup:** You can also run code at shutdown. In this case, this code will be executed **once**, **after** having handled possibly **many requests**.[1] That's useful for resources that you need to use for the whole app, and that are **shared** among requests, and/or that you need to **clean up** afterwards.[1]

**Example:** The excerpts I have don't include the lifespan code for loading an ML model. The closest example is from the SQL tutorial, which create[s] the tables on an application startup event[4]:

```python
app = FastAPI()

@app.on_event("startup")
def on_startup():
    create_db_and_tables()
```

You could put your model-loading code in a startup function like this. For the full lifespan example with a machine learning model, see the rest of the [Lifespan Events](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/events/) page, which continues past the "Use Case" section.
